By Jose Stell
Staff Writer

Los Gatos authorities
Monday had developed no
tangible leads into the slay-
ing of a 31-year-old free-
lance writer found just be-
fore midnight Friday in the
townhouse she shared with a
physician. :
Los Gatos Police Chief
Harold A. Johnson said rob-
bery and sexual assault have
been eliminated as motives.

Background checks are
being pursued on the victim,
Clara Louise Rose; Dr. Bar-
ry Slater, whose $100,000
Peach Willow Court home
she shared, and the victim’s
estranged husband, John
Rose of Hollister.

Lt. Robert Schuster said
Slater and Rose were ques-
tioned intensively and that
their alibis “washed.”

Slater was at a hospital
meeting when Mrs. Rose’s
assailant beat, choked and
shot her. Authorities believe
she had been dead several
hours before Slater returned
home to find her lying in a
pool of blood in the hallway.

Mrs. Rose’s ex-husband
was with their two daugh-
ters, Wendy and Shannon, at
his Hollister home when the

Dr. John Hauser, Santa
Clara County medical exam:
iner, said it appeared Mrs.
Rose was killed by two head
wounds from a gun fired at
close range, although she
also has been choked and
struck on the head with a
blunt object.

Hauser confirmed that the
victim had not been sexuall;
molested. She was fully
clothed when her body was
found.

Police would not say
whether Slater’s Los Gatos
Woods townhouse had been
broken into.
The residence in the Rin-
conada sector of Los Gatos
is one of numerous homes on
‘the private street, access to
which at one time was by
keycard entry and crossing
gate. They no longer have
that security.
Police said neighbors
were unable to offer any
clues. The only police calls
to that area have been occa-
sional disturbances created
by motorcyclists.

Mrs. Rose and Slater re-
portedly moved into the
townhouse with the children
several months ago.
